svg.aria-label: The real 29-claim chain re-drawn with each claim sized by how much is lost if it is removed; its 46 dependencies weighted the same way; the 29 that cost nothing alone removed one at a time to leave a 28-edge skeleton; and two further frames proposing a new claim and absorbing a new paper.

g.text: One theorem, and everything it rests on
29 claims and 46 dependencies — the object the rest of this act works on
this paper
another paper
a third
and so on
schematic
a claim both papers lean on
one node, not two — check it once and
everything above it inherits the check
Wish one
Papers stop being separate piles
because they land on the same claims
the graph program — 25
the MWIS dual — 11
the LP dual — 7
no active free signs — 4
claims lost if this one is removed
Which claims actually carry the load
remove one claim, recompute the closure, count what leaves — size is what is lost
sorted by what removing one costs
The same question, asked of every dependency
46 links, each weighted by what removing it costs
sorted by what removing one costs
29 cost nothing alone
Alone every one of these 29 is free
take them away together and 14 of the 29 claims leave the closure
The skeleton
28 dependencies, and every claim still reachable
this paper
another paper
a third
and so on
schematic
proposed
Wish two
A claim in a gap the structure names
a claim nobody has written yet
already checked — and it stays checked
a new paper
three new checks, not a hundred
Wish three
A new paper inherits what is checked
and only three of its claims are genuinely new
